sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Monroe Township, Gloucester County?
sections.html:
Monroe Township in Gloucester County, the Williamstown ZIP 08094 township, runs a resale certificate of occupancy inspection that the buyer's paperwork must accompany. Do not mix it up with the other Monroe Township in Middlesex County, which has a different office, fee chapter and appeal calendar.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 38,137 residents, and its 2020 to 2024 survey counts 14,116 households of about 2.65 people. Owners live in 85.2 percent of homes, with a median value of $283,100 and a median household income of $96,980. Workers average 31.7 minutes to their jobs, and 17.0 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: How did Monroe Township in Gloucester County take shape?
sections.html:
The legislature created the township on March 3, 1859, out of Washington Township, when the area still belonged to Camden County. It moved to Gloucester County on February 28, 1871 and was named for President James Monroe. In 1950 a section went to Winslow Township. The 2020 census count of 37,117 is the highest on record, after a 24.7 percent jump between 2000 and 2010.

The township covers 46.93 square miles, nearly all of it land, and is the second largest in the county by both area and population. Williamstown (15,082 people in 2020) and Victory Lakes (1,999) are the census designated places, and Berryland, Broad Lane, Cecil, Cross Keys, Downer, New Brooklyn and Radix are other place names. Neighbors are Clayton, Franklin, Glassboro and Washington Township in Gloucester County, Buena Vista Township and Folsom in Atlantic County, and Winslow Township in Camden County. The Hall Street School, built in 1887, was added to the National Register of Historic Places on September 27, 2006.

sections.h2: What does the Monroe resale inspection cost and how long does it take?
sections.html:
The Monroe Township Housing Office requires a resale certificate of occupancy application, and the township asks for it 3 to 4 weeks before settlement. A completed inspection is valid for only 60 days. The office is at 125 Virginia Avenue in Williamstown, reachable at 856-728-9800 ext. 289 or 296, and applications go in person or by mail.

Monroe Township Housing fee schedule on the resale application (revised August 3, 2026)
ItemFee
Resale inspection application$200
Request made less than 7 business days ahead$300
No answer at the door for a scheduled inspection$50
Reinspection$25
Reinspection requested less than 7 business days ahead$50
Affidavit for a temporary certificate of occupancy$100
Failure to obtain the resale certificate of occupancy$300

Source: Monroe Township Housing, Resale Application and Checklist.

Payment must be exact cash, a check or a money order payable to Monroe Township Housing. The office does not take credit or debit cards, and every fee is non-refundable. The buyer must also complete a notarized Acknowledgement of Responsibility, and inspections cannot be scheduled without it.

sections.h2: What does the Monroe resale checklist cover?
sections.html:
The checklist took effect August 3, 2026 and the township says it lists the full extent of the resale inspection.

  • House numbers at least 3 inches tall, on both sides of the mailbox.
  • Smoke detectors on every level, either ten-year sealed battery units or hardwired units under ten years old, and carbon monoxide detectors outside sleeping areas unless the house is all electric with a detached garage.
  • A 2A-10B:C fire extinguisher mounted and visible when leaving the kitchen, with a service tag from the last 12 months or a receipt for a new one.
  • For private wells, a satisfactory lab report that includes mercury. For private septic systems, a certification from the Gloucester County Department of Health.
  • Pool barriers with a 4 foot fence and a 4 foot gate that opens outward, closes itself and latches with the release 54 inches off the ground, plus working safety straps on hot tubs.
  • All zoning, construction and Board of Health permits and violations closed, and any abandoned property fees or emergency work charges paid.

sections.h2: What if the Monroe house needs repairs or has unpermitted work?
sections.html:
Section 162-11 of the township code lets a buyer of a dwelling that is unfit at transfer sign an affidavit listing the repairs needed. The affidavit lasts 60 days, work must start right after the sale, and the Housing Official can extend the period only for good cause. The buyer applies for the transfer before the scheduled closing, and the buyer can also assume the seller's duty to obtain the certificate by a written waiver filed with the Housing Department.

The township says a certificate is not a warranty. The buyer signs that acknowledgment and accepts responsibility for fixing violations or unpermitted work found later. The form recommends the buyer get a survey no more than 90 days old and file an OPRA request for permits with the Zoning and Construction Offices, and, where it applies, check for Pinelands Commission approval.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools look from a Monroe listing?
sections.html:
The Black Horse Pike crosses the township from northwest to southeast, carrying Route 42 in the northwest part and U.S. Route 322 in the southeast. Typical drive times run about 30 minutes to Philadelphia and 35 to Atlantic City, and the Atlantic City Expressway runs just outside its border. U.S. 322 on the west side reaches the New Jersey Turnpike in about 30 minutes. NJ Transit buses 315, 400 and 463 serve the area, and Cross Keys Airport is in the Cross Keys section.

Monroe Township Public Schools run six schools: Holly Glen, Oak Knoll, Radix and Whitehall elementary schools for kindergarten through grade 4, Williamstown Middle School for grades 5 to 8 and Williamstown High School. Enrollment was 5,736 in 2019-20. Students countywide can apply to the Gloucester County Institute of Technology in Deptford, which charges no tuition, and St. Mary School serves kindergarten through grade 8 under the Diocese of Camden.

sections.h2: How do Monroe appeals and recording fees work in Gloucester County?
sections.html:
Gloucester County uses an alternative assessment calendar, so the Board of Taxation takes appeals from November 15 through January 15, with a 4:00 pm cutoff on the last day for paper or online filings. Assessment postcards are mailed on or before November 15, and paper appeals need a check made out to the Gloucester County Board of Taxation. Online filing accepts credit cards.

The seller's state Realty Transfer Fee at the Census median value of $283,100 works out to $1,583.18 under the rates for sales up to $350,000: $600 for the first $150,000, $335 for the next $50,000 and $648.18 for the last $83,100.

Deeds are recorded with the Gloucester County Clerk, whose posted fee is $30 for the first page and $10 for each additional page. Since July 1, 2026 the Clerk's Office takes only money orders, checks or credit cards, checks of $10,000 or more must be certified, and out-of-state personal checks are not accepted. The Clerk's recording line is 856-853-3235.

faqs.q: How much is the Monroe Township resale certificate fee?
faqs.a: The Gloucester County township charges $200 for the resale inspection application, or $300 when the request comes less than seven business days before it is needed. A reinspection is $25, and the fees are not refundable.

faqs.q: How early should I apply for a Monroe resale certificate?
faqs.a: Apply 3 to 4 weeks before settlement. The township's inspection stays valid for 60 days, so time the visit to your settlement date, and the notarized buyer acknowledgment must be filed with the application.

faqs.q: Do I need a well test to sell a Monroe house on a private well?
faqs.a: Yes. The resale checklist requires a satisfactory lab report that includes mercury for a private well, and a Gloucester County Department of Health certification for a private septic system.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take on repairs after buying a Monroe house?
faqs.a: A buyer can sign an affidavit listing the repairs needed for legal occupancy. It lasts 60 days, repairs must begin right after the sale, and the buyer applies for the transfer before the closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Monroe assessment in Gloucester County?
faqs.a: The county's appeal window runs from November 15 to January 15, and filings must be in by 4:00 pm on January 15. Assessment postcards go out on or before November 15.
